title: Disputes between Sky Ecosystem participants are excluded from Resilience Fund coverage
content:
A.2.9.1.1.1.3.2 excludes five categories: prior or pending claims, "[c]laims between persons involved in the Sky Ecosystem," losses covered by other insurance, willful criminal offenses / fraud / dishonesty, and conflict of interest.

The intra-ecosystem exclusion is the structurally interesting one. It means the fund is directional: it finances defense against the outside world and never against another participant. Without it, Sky would be funding both sides of internal fights, and a well-resourced participant could weaponize a shared pool by suing a peer who then draws on the same fund to defend.

The exclusion only works because the Atlas provides an alternative venue — dispute resolution by the Core Council (A.2.8.1.1), which A.2.8.3.2.2 empowers to force Accord changes. Internal conflict is meant to be adjudicated inside the ecosystem, not litigated with ecosystem money. Read together, the exclusion is a channeling rule as much as a cost control.

The willful-criminality and conflict-of-interest exclusions carry an unresolved timing problem common to all such clauses: whether conduct was willful or conflicted is often the very question the litigation will decide, so applying the exclusion requires prejudging the case that the funding was requested to defend.
description: The exclusion list bars intra-ecosystem claims alongside prior claims, other-insured losses, willful criminality and conflicts of interest — so the fund funds defense against outsiders only.
